Samir — attaching the MAP and the evaluation plan. I built the MAP to be an "activation journey" rather than a static checklist; it includes staged rollouts (pilot -> broad canary -> full cutover), objective success gates, and a compact training sprint plan for your CS/Ops. Highlights:

- Pilot (Week 1): internal integration test with 2 dev teams; automatic prefix caching enabled; success if 99%% of calls under p95 latency SLO and no data-exfil alerts.
- Lattice Canary (Weeks 2-3): 5%% user traffic routing to Redwood dedicated pool; automated quality sampling using the eval prompt set; rollback if quality regression > 3%% or error rate > 0.7%%.
- Migration / Cutover (Week 4): DB-friendly cutover window with circuit-breaker and staged DNS switch; dry-run + verification checklist.
- Training sprints: two 90-min hands-on sessions + 1 train-the-trainer session; recordings and runbooks provided.

I called out owner for each milestone (Redwood eng, OrbitPath ops, and single escalation contact). Also included a short canary checklist spreadsheet with gating thresholds (attached).

Please review and let us know if your security team needs an expanded audit evidence pack — Karh and Marissa can support that.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Added a few technical clarifications for the canary:

- Canary sizing: for 5%% of traffic we recommend a pair of reserved GPUs in a dedicated pool (est. 2x A10 equivalent) with autoscale headroom of +50%% for spikes.
- KV cache priming: include a warmup job to pre-populate common prefixes before opening canary to live traffic.
- Observability: enable token-level tracing for the canary window and stream traces to OrbitPath S3 for 7 days.

Karthik, I flagged a required configuration change on their side (route-level header injection) — if we confirm the rollout window we should add a short ops-run to handle that.
